What Is RAG? Planning an AI Assistant for Business Knowledge

Understand retrieval-augmented generation and the data, permission and evaluation work behind a useful internal knowledge assistant.

By DevMania · 21 September 2026 · 2 min read
Share on LinkedInShare on WhatsApp

In this guide

Give the assistant relevant source materialClean the knowledge collectionEnforce permissions before retrievalMake answers inspectableEvaluate both retrieval and answers

Give the assistant relevant source material

Retrieval-augmented generation, often shortened to RAG, retrieves information and supplies it as context for a generated answer. In a business assistant, that material might be approved product guides or internal procedures. It is a way to connect answers with reference information, not a guarantee that every answer will be correct.

Clean the knowledge collection

Start with a small set of current documents. Remove duplicates, mark superseded versions and assign an owner to each policy. If the collection contains conflicting procedures, the assistant may retrieve the wrong one or combine incompatible information. Better retrieval cannot resolve an ownership decision the business has never made.

Enforce permissions before retrieval

A user should only retrieve material they are allowed to access. Do not fetch everything and ask the model to keep confidential sections secret. Apply access controls in the retrieval system and test them with users from different roles or companies. A natural-language instruction is not a substitute for authorization.

Make answers inspectable

Show references to the relevant source passages and allow the assistant to say that the supplied material is insufficient. For a product support example, test questions about discontinued items and missing specifications. The answer should not fill a gap with a plausible-sounding value. Keep a direct route to human support.

Evaluate both retrieval and answers

When an answer is wrong, check whether the right document was retrieved and whether the model used it correctly. Track these as different problems. Refresh the collection through a controlled process and repeat tests after updates. Begin with a narrow topic where the team can verify answers before expanding the knowledge base.

Turn planning into action. Create an editable website brief or work through the launch checklist.
